methodology_observations: OI and funding are read every minute and stored in five-minute steps.
Free/guest Research views are approximately 15 minutes delayed.
TradRadar describes 0.01 percent per eight hours as approximately normal and flags above 0.015 percent on at least half of exchanges as overheated long funding.

spot_context.note: Separate hourly spot aggregate; not synchronized with derivatives observations.

comparison.rule: Do not average or blend these provider totals. Reconcile contract IDs, multipliers, quote currencies, coin-margined versus stablecoin-margined instruments, mark-price conversion and event timestamps directly from exchange-native endpoints.

interpretation.funding: Both publishers display +0.01 percent per eight hours. TradRadar describes this as approximately normal; it is not by itself an extreme-funding signal.
interpretation.positioning: TradRadar reports 76.2 percent long accounts and a 3.21 account ratio, not position notional.
interpretation.liquidations: The reported short-liquidation lower bound exceeds the long-liquidation lower bound. This is compatible with short covering, while the high long-account share indicates one-sided account positioning; neither establishes direction.
interpretation.conclusion: Provider disagreement is a data-quality blocker, not a reason to choose the larger or smaller estimate.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Different contract sets, quote currencies, multipliers or conversion methods explain part of the OI gap.
supporting_evidence: Kodexius reports seven contracts across five exchanges and exposes USDT/USDC contracts separately on Binance and Bybit.
TradRadar aggregates seven exchanges without exposing the exact XRP contract list.
disconfirming_evidence_required: Exchange-native contract-by-contract data reconciles both providers under a common unit and cutoff.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Different update times and TradRadar's stated guest delay contribute to the observed gap.
supporting_evidence: TradRadar page updated 12:45 UTC and states a 15-minute guest delay.
disconfirming_evidence_required: Both series reconstructed at the same exchange event-time cutoff still materially disagree.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Mark-price, quote conversion or aggregation logic differs.
supporting_evidence: No raw inputs or reproducible per-contract calculation is exposed.
Four overlapping venue aggregates differ materially.
disconfirming_evidence_required: Both providers' calculations reconcile with exchange-native raw responses.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Short liquidations may have contributed to the move while the account population remains long-skewed.
supporting_evidence: Short liquidation lower bound USD 3.60M versus USD 1.75M long.
disconfirming_evidence_required: Synchronized exchange-native liquidation and notional-position data show no such skew.

source_independence.note: Separate dashboards share upstream exchanges. Fuelmaps is spot-only and included only as unsynchronized context.

reasons: No byte-complete raw exchange or publisher receipts.
No independent timestamp anchors or exchange-native event timestamps.
Different contract universes and undisclosed conversion details.
Account-count positioning and liquidation lower bounds are not notional/complete-flow measures.
Spot depth is unsynchronized and from a separate publisher.

next_actions: Capture exchange-native XRP perpetual OI per instrument with contract ID, multiplier, quote currency, mark/index price, event timestamp and local receipt timestamp.
Normalize USD notional with a documented timestamped conversion price; keep coin-margined and stablecoin-margined contracts separate.
Reconcile Binance, Bybit, Hyperliquid and OKX contract by contract before adding Gate, Bitget, MEXC and HTX.
Capture exchange-native funding and liquidation streams at matching cutoffs.
Keep provider values separate; do not backfill them into a single OI series.
Do not issue a directional forecast from this snapshot.
